verified.claim: California taxes capital gains at ordinary income rates; there is no lower state rate.

title: Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses

verified.claim: Federal long-term capital gains are taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% depending on taxable income.
verified.quote: A capital gains rate of 15% applies if your taxable income is: ... more than $96,700 but less than or equal to $600,050 for married filing jointly ... However, a capital gains rate of 20% applies to the extent that your taxable income exceeds the thresholds set for the 15% capital gain rate.

verified.claim: Depreciation taken on rental real estate is taxed at up to 25% when the property is sold (unrecaptured section 1250 gain).
verified.quote: The portion of any unrecaptured section 1250 gain from selling section 1250 real property is taxed at a maximum 25% rate.

verified.claim: A loss on the sale of personal-use property such as a home is not deductible.
verified.quote: Losses from the sale of personal-use property, such as your home or car, aren't tax deductible.

title: Topic no. 559, Net investment income tax

verified.claim: A 3.8% net investment income tax applies above $250,000 (joint) / $200,000 (single) of modified AGI.
verified.quote: the NIIT is 3.8 percent on the lesser of: the net investment income, or the excess of modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) over the following threshold amounts: $250,000 for married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse ... $200,000 for single or head of household

verified.claim: Net investment income includes interest, dividends, rents and gains on real estate and securities.
verified.quote: net investment income for purpose of this tax, includes, but isn't limited to: interest, dividends, certain annuities, royalties, and rents ... net gains from the disposition of property such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and real estate

title: Topic no. 701, Sale of your home

verified.claim: Up to $250,000 ($500,000 joint) of gain on a main home can be excluded after owning and living in it for 2 of the last 5 years.
verified.quote: you may qualify to exclude up to $250,000 of that gain from your income, or up to $500,000 of that gain if you file a joint return with your spouse ... If you or your spouse owned the home for at least 24 months (2 years) out of the last 5 years leading up to the date of the sale, you meet the ownership test.

verified.claim: The federal deduction for state and local taxes (including property tax) is capped at $40,000 for 2025, shrinking above $500,000 of income but not below $10,000.
verified.quote: The overall limit on the deduction for state and local income, sales, and property taxes has increased to $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately). The overall limit is reduced if your modified adjusted gross income is more than $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately) but will not be reduced below $10,000
